original_question: Let K be a number field, let f (x) ∈ K(x) be a rational function of degree at least 2, and let α ∈ K be a point that is not periodic for f . Then (f, α) is eventually stable over K. One might be bold and ask if there is a uniform bound for the eventual stability predicted by Conjecture 19.4, but some care is needed,  since it is not hard to see that for any k ≥ 1, the constant C f (x), f k (α) in Definition 19.2 must be at least k.
target_in_paper: Question 19.5 in Section 19, read together with Definition 19.2 and the sentence immediately following Conjecture 19.4. Your draft begins with Conjecture 19.4, but its real aim is the paper's sharper uniform-boundedness question for eventual stability after excluding the obvious shift obstruction. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft correctly places the problem in the Section 19 setting: K is a number field, f(x) is a rational function over K of degree at least 2, and α is a K-rational point. It also reproduces Conjecture 19.4 almost verbatim and correctly notices the paper's warning that naive uniformity fails because the constants C(f,f^k(α)) must be at least k. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
missing_details: The nearest official target is not Conjecture 19.4 itself, but Question 19.5, which asks for a uniform bound κ(d,K) on the factor counts in statement (19.1). ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Question 19.5 fixes an exact degree d≥2 and ranges over degree-d maps; your draft only says 'degree at least 2,' which is too loose for the paper's uniform formulation. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The official hypothesis is that α is wandering, meaning its forward orbit O_f(α) is infinite, not merely that α is non-periodic. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Question 19.5 adds the crucial extra assumption f^{-1}(α)∩P^1(K)=∅, which is the paper's way to avoid the trivial obstruction mentioned immediately before the question. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

To make the problem stand-alone, one must define the iterates by writing f^n(x)=F_n(x)/G_n(x) with F_n,G_n∈K[x] relatively prime. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The quantity to be uniformly bounded is the number of irreducible factors of F_n(x)-αG_n(x) in K[x], counted with multiplicity, for every n≥1; this is the paper's statement (19.1). ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The paper's official question also includes two refinements omitted from the draft: whether one may take κ(2,Q)=3, and whether κ can depend only on d and [K:Q]. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

As written, the draft is a statement plus commentary, not a stand-alone research question. The paper's corresponding formulation is explicitly interrogative. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
refined_question: Let K be a number field and let d≥2. For a rational function f(x)∈K(x) of degree d, write its nth iterate as f^n(x)=F_n(x)/G_n(x) with relatively prime polynomials F_n,G_n∈K[x]. Let α∈K be a wandering point for f, i.e. O_f(α) is infinite, and assume that f^{-1}(α)∩P^1(K)=∅. Is there a constant κ(d,K) such that, for every such pair (f,α) and every n≥1, the polynomial F_n(x)-αG_n(x) has at most κ(d,K) irreducible factors in K[x], counted with multiplicity? In particular, when d=2 and K=Q, can one take κ(2,Q)=3? More generally, if K is a number field, can the same statement hold with κ depending only on d and [K:Q]? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
justification: The first sentence of the draft is Conjecture 19.4 almost word-for-word, but the second sentence immediately pivots to the stronger issue of a uniform bound and repeats the cautionary lead-in that introduces Question 19.5. So the closest paper-faithful target is Question 19.5, not the broader Conjecture 19.4 alone. Definition 19.2 supplies the precise factor-count formulation used in that question, and Example 19.3 explains why the paper singles out the case κ(2,Q)=3. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
